sections.body:
Open to anyone (no credentials needed). Creates an account and its profile in one transaction.

```json
{
  "email": "required, must not belong to another account (compared ignoring case)",
  "password": "required, checked by Django's password validators",
  "display_name": "optional, a slug of at most 50 characters, must be unused; default user-<id>"
}
```

- `201` with the new account: `id`, `email`, `is_public` and `profile` (see `GET /api/auth/me/`).
- `400` with the field errors (invalid email, email in use, weak password, display name taken or not a slug). Nothing is stored.
sections.heading: `POST /api/auth/register/`

sections.body: Open to anyone. The simplejwt `TokenObtainPairView`: send `email` and `password`; the answer is `200` with `access` and `refresh` tokens. Wrong credentials: `401`. The access token goes in the `Authorization: Bearer ...` header of every other endpoint.
sections.heading: `POST /api/auth/token/`

sections.body: Open to anyone. The simplejwt `TokenRefreshView`: send `refresh`; the answer is `200` with a new `access` token. An invalid or expired refresh token: `401`. Whether a new refresh token is returned is unknown from the repository code read here (`ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS` is false).
sections.heading: `POST /api/auth/token/refresh/`

sections.body: Authenticated (JWT, or the browser session cookie). Returns the caller's account: `id`, `email`, `is_public` and `profile` with `display_name`, `date_of_birth`, `sex`, `ethnicity`, `height_cm`, `is_public` and `social_handles` (each `platform`, `handle`, `url`). Without valid credentials: `401`.
sections.heading: `GET /api/auth/me/`

sections.body: Open to anyone, no credentials read. Returns the profile with the same fields as `profile` above. The profile is returned only when both the profile and its account are public; otherwise `404` (a private profile and an unknown name look the same).
sections.heading: `GET /api/profiles/<display_name>/`

sections.body:
The API accepts either a JWT (`Authorization: Bearer ...`) or the browser sign-in session
cookie. A session request that changes data (POST, PATCH, DELETE) must also send the
`X-CSRFToken` header with the value of the `csrftoken` cookie, otherwise the answer is `403`
and nothing is stored. A request with no valid credentials is still refused with `401`.
sections.heading: Browser access

sections.body:
Creates a report with `origin = manual`, owned by the caller, and all its results in one
transaction.

```json
{
  "laboratory": "optional, applies to results that name none",
  "results": [
    {
      "loinc_code": "required, must be a stored analyte",
      "reported_value": "required, decimal as a string, at most 6 decimals",
      "reported_unit": "required, as the lab reported it",
      "laboratory": "optional", "method": "optional", "device": "optional",
      "collected_at": "optional ISO 8601 with UTC offset",
      "reported_at": "optional ISO 8601 with UTC offset"
    }
  ]
}
```

- `201` with the report and its results. Each result has the stored fields,
  `validation_state` (`entered`), `aggregation_eligible` (true only with laboratory,
  method and a confirmed state, see below), `normalised_value` / `normalised_unit` (empty unless a stored conversion
  exists) and `plausibility`.
- `400` if any result is invalid (unknown LOINC code, more than 6 decimals, DEXA or
  microbiome without laboratory and method, naive time, ...). The body names the result
  index and field, e.g. `{"results": {"1": {"reported_value": ["..."]}}}`; nothing is stored.
- `401` when not logged in.
sections.heading: `POST /api/labs/reports/`

sections.body:
- `reported_value` is at most **40 characters** (after trimming); longer gives a 400 naming
  `reported_value` and the result index.
- A report holds at most **200 results**; more gives a 400 naming `results`, before anything is stored.

These are abuse protection, not scientific limits: a 20-digit value with 6 decimals needs far
fewer than 40 characters. In both cases nothing is stored. Defaults are open in Q70.
sections.heading: Input limits

sections.body: The report with its results. `404` for a report owned by someone else.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/`

sections.body:
The report as a FHIR R4 `collection` Bundle (`application/fhir+json`): one DiagnosticReport whose
`result` references one Observation per result, plus an Organization (name only) per distinct
laboratory. Each Observation has the LOINC code and the value as reported (a JSON number, not
rounded). `valueQuantity` has `system` `http://unitsofmeasure.org` and `code` only when the
reported unit exactly equals a stored `Unit.ucum_code`; otherwise only `unit` text. `method`,
`performer` (laboratory), `effectiveDateTime` (collected) and `issued` (reported) appear only
when stored. `status` is `unknown` and no patient is referenced (Q73). `404` for another user's
report; `401`/`403` when not signed in. Element sources: docs/fhir/lab-report-mapping.md.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/fhir/`

sections.body:
The report's results as OMOP CDM v5.4 MEASUREMENT-shaped rows (JSON only, no CSV yet):
`{"omop_cdm_version": "5.4", "columns": [...], "rows": [...]}`. `columns` is the DDL order
(`core.omop.MEASUREMENT_COLUMNS`); there is one row per result, ordered by result id, each built
only by `lab_result_to_omop_measurement` with every column present. Retracted results are not
exported; disputed and entered ones are (the export is the owner's own data, Q80). Every
`*_concept_id`, `person_id` and other column without a stored, cited source is `null`: no
vocabulary content is stored, so none is invented (Q69). `404` for another user's report;
`401`/`403` when not signed in. Column sources: docs/omop/measurement-mapping.md.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/omop/`

sections.body:
Shows one of your results in the UCUM unit you name. The original value and unit are always
kept and always returned; nothing is written. `unit` is required, at most 64 characters, and
must be a stored UCUM code (otherwise `400` naming `unit`). Response:
`{result_id, reported_value, reported_unit, value, unit, converted, reason, conversion_source}`;
decimals are strings, not rounded.

- `converted: true`: a stored, sourced conversion exists (an analyte-specific one is preferred);
  `value` is `reported_value` times its factor, `unit` is the requested unit and
  `conversion_source` is the stored Source (`id, name, version, licence, url, retrieved_at`).
- `converted: false, reason: "same_unit"`: the requested unit is the reported one.
- `converted: false, reason: "no_conversion_known"`: no stored direct conversion (an inverse or
  a chain is never used) or the reported unit is not stored; `value`/`unit` are the reported
  ones.

Retracted results can still be viewed by their owner (Q81). `404` for another user's result;
`401`/`403` when not signed in.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/results/<id>/convert/?unit=<ucum>`

sections.body:
Places one of your results against three separate ranges, never merged:
`{result_id, reported_value, reported_unit, reference_range, optimal_range, safety_threshold,
comparison_value, comparison_unit, converted, conversion_source}`. Each range object has `status` and, when a range applies,
`low`, `high` (decimal strings, `null` = open), `unit` and `source` (`name, version, url`).

- Comparison value: `reported_value` if reported in the analyte's unit, else the stored
  `normalised_value` (only when it is in that unit), else none. Nothing is converted on the fly. `converted` is `true` when the stored normalised
  value was used; `conversion_source` is then that stored Source (`name, version, url`), else `null`.
  A lab+method tier is chosen only among rows that apply to the subject, so a stratified
  lab-specific row never hides a generic row.
- Status rule: `below` if value < low, `above` if value > high, `inside` otherwise (bounds
  inclusive, a null bound is open); `no_range` if none applies (no bounds returned);
  `not_comparable` (`reason: "no_value_in_analyte_unit"`) when there is no comparison value.
- `reference_range` adds `lab, method, population, evidence_grade`. Only rows in the analyte's
  unit whose lab and method are empty or equal (trimmed, casefolded) to the result's apply;
  rows matching lab and method beat generic ones; a tie gives `no_range`.
- `optimal_range` is shown only if `displayable_optimal_range` passes (source, population,
  endpoint, evidence grade and last-reviewed date all present); it adds `population, endpoint,
  evidence_grade, last_reviewed`.
- `safety_threshold`: exactly one row is used; several give `no_range` with
  `reason: "ambiguous_several_thresholds"`.

The subject is unknown (no age, sex or ancestry stored), so only unstratified rows apply (Q82).
Retracted results can still be viewed by their owner. `404` for another user's result;
`401`/`403` when not signed in.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/results/<id>/ranges/`

sections.body:
`plausibility = {"status": "within" | "outside" | "not_checked", "range_source": {...} | null}`.
It compares the value only with a stored, cited `ReferenceRange` of the same analyte whose
unit equals the reported unit (or the normalised unit). Only a single range without age,
sex, ancestry or population strata, and whose lab and method are empty or equal to the result's, is used; otherwise the status is `not_checked`. It is a flag: the
value is stored in every case. No range is invented or seeded (Q70).
sections.heading: Plausibility

sections.body:
Header (UTF-8, comma-separated): `loinc_code,value,unit,collected_at,reported_at,laboratory,method`.
The first three columns are required; the last four are optional. Any other or duplicate column
rejects the whole file with a `400` naming the header. Empty cells are treated as absent.
Rows go through the same rules as manual entry. Nothing is guessed (Q71).
sections.heading: CSV import (two steps)

sections.body:
Multipart field `file`. Stores nothing. Returns
`{"rows": [{"row": 1, "status": "recognised" | "not_recognised", "reason": "", "loinc_code", "value", "unit", "plausibility"}]}`
with `row` the 1-based data line. `not_recognised` carries a reason naming the column (unknown
LOINC code, empty unit, bad number, time without UTC offset, ...) and `plausibility` null. The
status `inferred` exists in the review vocabulary but this parser never emits it.
sections.heading: `POST /api/labs/imports/csv/preview/`

sections.body:
Same file again, plus an optional `laboratory` form field for the report. If any row is
`not_recognised` the answer is `400` with `detail` and the `rows`, and nothing is stored.
Otherwise one `LabReport` (`origin = import`, `import_name` = file name) and its results are
stored in one transaction, with `validation_state = user_confirmed` (you checked every row in
the preview); `201` with the report and results.

The report JSON (confirm, `GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/`) carries `original_retained` (bool),
`original_sha256` and `original_size` (bytes). The uploaded CSV is kept exactly as sent, in a
private store under a generated name (never your file name), with no automatic expiry (Q57).
It is never served, published or put into OpenData: no endpoint returns the file, a path or a
URL. `DELETE /api/labs/reports/<id>/` removes the file after the rollback commits (Q65). If you
send `redact_terms`, the original is **not** kept (it would defeat the redaction): the confirm
answer has `original_retained: false` and `original_not_retained_reason` (Q76). The preview
never stores a file; a refused confirm leaves none.
sections.heading: `POST /api/labs/imports/csv/confirm/`

sections.body:
| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `entered` | typed or imported, not yet checked (typed entries start here) |
| `user_confirmed` | the user checked it against their own report |
| `source_verified` | the original document is attached and the value matches it (deterministic extraction or a second person) |
| `disputed` | flagged as possibly wrong |
| `retracted` | withdrawn by the user, excluded from statistics, kept for audit |

A result is `aggregation_eligible` only with a laboratory, a method **and** the state
`user_confirmed` or `source_verified`. The owner changes the state with
`{"validation_state": "<state>"}`: `user_confirmed`, `disputed` or `retracted` give `200`
with the result as in `GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/`. `entered` and `source_verified` (no
attached-original check exists yet), and any change away from `retracted`, give `400` naming
`validation_state`. Another user's or a missing result gives `404`. Nothing changes on `400`/`404`.
sections.heading: Validation states and `PATCH /api/labs/results/<id>/validation/`

sections.body:
Off by default. Both import endpoints accept an optional `redact_terms`: the exact strings to
remove (your name, IDs), as repeated multipart fields, one JSON list, or a JSON array. At most
20 terms, each 1..200 characters and not blank; a breach gives `400` naming `redact_terms` and
nothing is stored. Matching is exact and case-insensitive. Overlapping or adjacent matches merge into one
removal (one placeholder) naming the term with the longest match, so no part of a longer
match is kept. There are no built-in patterns (Q72). Each removal becomes `[REDACTED]`. The
terms may match at most 1000 places in a file, otherwise `400` naming `redact_terms`. Row
count and field lengths are checked on the raw file before redaction runs (`400` naming `file`).
If a cell only exceeds its limit because `[REDACTED]` is longer than the term, the `400` names
`redact_terms`. Cells are trimmed before they are checked and redacted, so offsets are relative to the trimmed cell.

Redaction is applied cell by cell to the data rows, to the file name (`import_name`) and to the
`laboratory` form field, before the rows are evaluated; the header is not touched. The preview
answers `redaction: {"applied": bool, "removals": [{"row", "column", "term_index", "start",
"end", "line", "replacement"}]}`. `row` is the data line (null for the file name and form
field), `start`/`end`/`line` locate the match inside that field, and `term_index` is the
position in your list. The removed text is never echoed back. Confirm re-applies the same terms,
so only the placeholder is stored. A term that hits `loinc_code`, `value`, `unit`, `collected_at`
or `reported_at` makes that row `not_recognised` naming the column (a value is never silently
changed), so confirm refuses. Without `redact_terms`, `applied` is `false` and nothing changes.
sections.heading: PII redaction (opt-in)

sections.body:
File at most 1 MiB; at most 200 data rows; each field at most its model length (`value` 40
characters); the file must be UTF-8.
sections.heading: Limits (`400` naming the limit, nothing stored)

sections.body:
Rolls back an import: removes the report and its results, nothing else. `204`; `404` for another
user's report; `409` for a manual report. The retained original file is not stored yet (TG-g).
sections.heading: `DELETE /api/labs/reports/<id>/`

sections.body:
PhenoAge (Levine 2018) computed from the nine analytes of one of your reports (TG-i part 2).
`age_years` is a request parameter and is never stored (Q79); a missing value, or one that is not a
finite number or is too large to fit one (for example `1e400`), is `400` naming `age_years`. Another user's or a missing report is `404`; anonymous is 401/403.
Each analyte is found by the LOINC code of its biomarker; `retracted` and `disputed` results are
ignored. The value is used as is when its UCUM unit equals the PhenoAge unit, otherwise only a
stored unit conversion is applied. Nothing is written.

`200` with the result: `{"phenoage_years", "mortality_score", "xb", "constants_version",
"inputs": [{"field", "lab_result_id", "value", "unit", "converted"}], "method"}`; or `200` with
`{"refusal": {"reason", "field"}}`. Reasons: `analyte_not_mapped` (no verified LOINC code for
the analyte; **currently every analyte, see Q79**), `missing_input`, `ambiguous_analyte` (two
usable results for one analyte), `unit_not_convertible` (no stored conversion), and the engine's
`not_finite_input`, `crp_not_positive`, `mortality_score_out_of_range`.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/phenoage/?age_years=<number>`

sections.body:
Calculated quotient markers for one of your reports (TG-n part 1). Each stored
`CalculatedRatioDefinition` (numerator and denominator analyte, the UCUM unit each input must be
in, and a cited Source) is computed in code with `Decimal` (28 digits, half-even, not rounded).
No definition is seeded (Q83), so until some are stored the answer is
`{"report_id", "markers": [], "note": "no_definitions_stored"}`. Another user's or a missing
report is `404`; anonymous is 401/403. Only this report's results are used; `retracted` and
`disputed` results are ignored; a value is used as reported when its unit matches, otherwise only
a stored unit conversion applies. Nothing is written.

Each marker has `name`, `calculated: true` and `source`. Computed: `status: "computed"`, `value`
(string), `unit_note` (the two input units; no unit is invented for the ratio) and `inputs`
(`role`, `lab_result_id`, `loinc_code`, `value_used`, `unit_used`, `reported_value`,
`reported_unit`, `collected_at`, `reported_at`, `converted`, `conversion_source` — the stored conversion's Source, null when not converted). Otherwise `status: "not_computable"`,
`value: null` and `reasons`: `missing_input:<role>`, `ambiguous_input:<role>`,
`unit_not_convertible:<role>`, `denominator_zero`.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/calculated/`

sections.body:
Completeness and freshness per organ system (TG-h part 1). Each stored `OrganSystemPanel` (a name,
its expected analytes and a cited Source) is listed, ordered by name. No panel is seeded (Q84),
so until some are stored the answer is `{"panels": []}`. Anonymous is 401/403. Only your own
results count, across all of your reports; `retracted` and `disputed` results are ignored.
Nothing is written.

Each panel has `name`, `source`, `expected_count`, `present_count`, `present` and `missing`
(`biomarker_id`, `loinc_code`), `last_collected_at` (newest `collected_at`, else `reported_at`;
null when no present result has a date), `age_days` (whole days from that date to now, or null) and
`sparse` (true when `present_count < expected_count`). A panel with no expected analytes is 0/0,
not sparse, with a null date.
sections.heading: `GET /api/labs/completeness/`

sections.body:
Owner-only (JWT). `GET` returns the plain-language notice (copies already cloned by others are outside the instance's control), what is deleted, and the two choices; `keep_for_research` is marked `available: false` with its reason.

`POST` with `choice` = `delete_everything` and `confirm` = `true` deletes the user, profile, lab reports, results, measurements and the retained original files in one transaction (files are removed once it commits). Without `confirm` true, or with an unknown choice: 400, nothing deleted. `keep_for_research`: 409 "de-identification not implemented yet", nothing deleted. Unauthenticated: 401. Defaults: Q85.
sections.heading: `GET|POST /api/auth/me/erase/` (account erasure)

sections.body:
Owner-only (JWT, then session with CSRF, as the CSV import). Multipart `file` (at most 5 MiB) and optional `profile_id`. Reads a plain-JSON get-based single-client export or all-clients bundle, both `version` 2, or an unencrypted full browser backup (`format` `labcharts-backup`, `version` 1; the profile ids are its `profileId`s, and the response `container` is `browser backup`) (`docs/ecosystem/getbased-archive-format.md`). **Stores nothing**: no report, no result, no retained original; the archive content is not logged.

A bundle with several profiles and no `profile_id` returns `{"status": "choose_profile", "profile_ids": [...]}` and no rows. Otherwise `{"status": "preview", "rows": [...], "summary": {...}, "can_confirm": bool}`. Each row: `marker`, `value` (exact text, `0.10` stays `0.10`), `date`, `status` (`matched` | `not_recognised` | `not_imported`), `reason`, and for a matched row `loinc_code`, `unit` (UCUM), `mapping_source`, `mapping_source_url` and `unit_source` (`path@sha` of the get-based catalogue unit), plus `flags` (AI-read, may be AI-read, origin not shown, origin unknown, edited in get-based after import; model and provider are entry-level and qualified). Matching is only through a stored `GetbasedMarkerMapping` row, never by name; with an empty table every marker is "not recognised". `can_confirm` is true only with no not recognised row and at least one matched row; left-out rows (deleted, calculated) are counted in `summary` and do not block.

400: not UTF-8, not JSON, `getbased-migration`, a version other than 2 (a `labcharts-backup` other than 1: the message names the version found and the supported one), an encrypted `labcharts-backup` (`encrypted: true` or a `v1:` value: "still locked with the get-based passphrase"), an unknown `profile_id`, or a file over the bound; the message names the found format/version and the supported ones. Unauthenticated: 401. Defaults: Q100.
sections.heading: `POST /api/labs/imports/getbased/preview/` (get-based archive preview)

sections.body:
Owner-only, same authentication, upload bounds and refusals as the preview (5 MiB, `version` exactly 2 (backup: exactly 1, unencrypted only), no migration archive, 1000 entries, 5000 values); send the same `file` and `profile_id` again. A bundle with more than one profile needs a `profile_id`. **400** listing the rows (`rows`, each with its reason) while any row is not recognised (no mapping, unit not verified, bad date, not a number), or when no row is matched, or when the shared result rules refuse a value: nothing is stored. Rows left out as calculated (deny-list, `calculatedRatios`, `derivedFrom`) or deleted do not block. **201**: `{"report_id", "stored_count", "left_out": {"calculated", "deleted"}, "original_retained": false, "original_not_retained_reason"}`.

One `LabReport` is stored with `origin` `import`, `import_source` `getbased`, `import_format` (`getbased-export`, `getbased-database` or `getbased-labcharts-backup`), `import_format_version` 2 (1 for the backup) and `import_name` = the fixed name `getbased-export.json` (the upload's file name is not kept, because it can carry the client's name), plus one `LabResult` per matched row: the exact archive number, the mapping's cited unit, `collected_at` empty, `validation_state` `entered` and `aggregation_eligible` false. The owner confirms each result through `PATCH /api/labs/results/<id>/validation/`. Identity, chat, nutrition, wallet and credentials are never stored or logged, and the original file is not kept. Undo: `DELETE /api/labs/reports/<id>/` removes the report, its results and their provenance.

`GET /api/labs/reports/<id>/` returns `import_source`, `import_format`, `import_format_version` and, for each result, `getbased_provenance` (null for results not from get-based): `flag` and `flag_text`, `manually_edited` and `edited_label` ("edited in get-based after import"), `entry_date`, `has_marker_sources`, `marker_sources` (`reported`, `file`, `at` verbatim, `snapshot_id`) and `imported_with` (`model_id`, `provider`, each "unknown" when empty, and the qualifier "last import into this date; the model for this value is unknown"; entry-level, not proof of the model of this value). Defaults: Q101, Q102.
sections.heading: `POST /api/labs/imports/getbased/confirm/` (get-based archive confirm)

sections.body:
`GET` lists your protocols. `POST` creates a protocol in `draft` (`201`) from `title` plus any facets, `level`, `in_effect_since` (date), `history` (`analytic` default, or `synthesized`) and `lineage_note` (only with `history=synthesized`, else `400`). A draft response has `missing`: what is still absent in plain words (for example "No efficacy markers yet."); it never blocks the save. `origin` is `community` by default; `curated` is `403` unless the user is staff.

Already running: `already_running: true` needs `in_effect_since` (today or earlier) and `level`; it sets `tracked_since` to today, state `active`, and creates version 1 with reason "imported as already running" followed by your optional `reason` text. The response has `notes` saying that adding past measurements is invited, not required.
sections.heading: `GET|POST /api/protocols/`

sections.body:
`GET` returns the protocol, `latest_version` (null in draft). `PATCH` while `draft` edits in place: no version, no reason, `in_effect_since`, `history` and `lineage_note` can change. Moving `state` to `active` leaves draft: it creates version 1 and needs a non-blank `reason` and a `level`, else `400` and the protocol stays `draft`. After that every change of `title`, `level`, `state` or a facet creates version N+1 with one change event per changed field, and a non-blank `reason` is mandatory (`400`, nothing created). A request that changes nothing is `400`. Allowed state moves: draft to active; active to paused or completed; paused to active or completed. The response has the protocol and, when one was created, `version`. Correcting the latest version is a new version, never an edit of it.

Heightened acknowledgment: moving to `active` (from `draft`, from `paused`, or through `already_running` on `POST`) is `400` (`acknowledge`, nothing created) when the protocol `level` is `research` or any item has `provenance: animal-derived`, unless the body has `acknowledge: true` (any other value is `400`). The error text includes the statement. With it, one append-only `ActivationAcknowledgment` is written in the same transaction (protocol, version, actor, time, level, the animal-derived item names, the statement shown). Resuming from `paused` asks again. On an already `active` protocol, an edit that newly makes it `research` or adds an animal-derived item name needs the same `acknowledge: true` (otherwise `400`) and logs one row; edits that add no new reason ask for nothing.
sections.heading: `GET|PATCH /api/protocols/<id>/`

sections.body: Every version, oldest first: `number`, `created_at`, `actor`, `reason`, `snapshot` (the tracked fields) and `events`: `[{field, old, new, timestamp, actor, reason}]`. `field` is a path such as `interventions[0].amount` or `state`.
sections.heading: `GET /api/protocols/<id>/versions/`

sections.body: One version. Read-only: there is no update or delete route, `PATCH`, `PUT` and `DELETE` return `405`, and the version stays as it was. In code, `save()` on an existing row, queryset `update()` and `delete()` raise.
sections.heading: `GET /api/protocols/<id>/versions/<number>/`

sections.body: Owner-only. For the protocol as it stands now (Draft, or the latest version), the per-day total of **label contents** per substance. For each item with a `product_id` and `units_per_day`, each ingredient with a declared amount adds `amount_per_unit x units_per_day`, computed with `Decimal`, and only ingredients with exactly the same unit string are added together; different units are listed as separate totals and never converted (Q131). Response: `{protocol, kind: "label-contents-total", note, substances, items_without_units_per_day}`. Each substance has `totals` (`{unit, amount, contributions}`; a contribution has the product, its `label_source`, the ingredient's `ingredient_label_source`, `amount_per_unit`, `units_per_day`, `per_day`) and `without_amount`: ingredients whose label gives no amount, listed with `amount: null`, never summed and never estimated. Items with a product but no `units_per_day` are listed and contribute nothing. The response has no posology or dose field: it is a total of what the labels declare, not a recommendation. Totals follow the product's current label data. Left out: the intake schedule, the restock projection and the dose sanity check on the sum (no cited thresholds, Q126).
sections.heading: `GET /api/protocols/<id>/ingredient-totals/`

sections.body: Deterministic field-level diff of two versions (stdlib `difflib`, no AI). Returns `facets` (`interventions` = name and schedule, `doses` = amount and unit per intervention, `cycles`, `measures`), each `{changed, unified}` with unified diff lines over the canonical JSON, and `changes`: `[{field, old, new}]`, for example `{"field": "doses[0].amount", "old": "6", "new": "8"}`. Missing or non-numeric `from`/`to` is `400`; an unknown version is `404`.
sections.heading: `GET /api/protocols/<id>/diff/?from=<n>&to=<m>`

sections.body: `GET` lists substances with their codes. `POST` (staff) creates one from `name`, optional `substance_class` and an optional `codes` list; any invalid code refuses the whole request (`400`, nothing created). Returns `201`.
sections.heading: `GET|POST /api/substances/`

sections.body: `GET` returns one substance, `404` if unknown. `PATCH` (staff) changes `name` and `substance_class`; codes are changed through the code routes.
sections.heading: `GET|PATCH /api/substances/<id>/`

sections.body: Staff only. Adds one code (`201`). The same system and code twice on one substance is `400`.
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/<id>/codes/`

sections.body: Staff only. Corrects a code. The result must still have a source and a fetch date, or it is `400`. Changing `code`, `system` or `source` needs a new `fetched_on` in the same request (`400` otherwise). The same goes for `substance_class` or `class_source` on `PATCH /api/substances/<id>/`, which need `class_fetched_on`. Text fields refuse NUL characters with `400`.
sections.heading: `PATCH /api/substances/<id>/codes/<code_id>/`

sections.body: Owner-only (any signed-in user, for their own products; another user's product is `404`, anonymous is `401` or `403`). Nothing is seeded. A product is `{id, name, label_source, label_fetched_on, ingredients}`: `label_source` (what the label is, up to 300 characters) and `label_fetched_on` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, not in the future) are required, so a product without a label source is `400`. An ingredient is `{id, substance, amount_per_unit, unit, label_source}`: `substance` is the id of an existing substance, `amount_per_unit` a plain ASCII decimal string (at most 18 digits before and 12 after the point; anything that would need rounding is `400`) or `null` when the label gives none, `unit` is required with an amount, and `label_source` is required. A substance can appear once per product. Unknown fields are `400`. Product ingredients feed `GET /api/protocols/<id>/ingredient-totals/` (docs/api-protocols.md).
sections.heading: Products and declared ingredients (TG-e)

sections.body: `GET` lists your products with their ingredients. `POST` creates one (`201`) from `name`, `label_source` and `label_fetched_on`.
sections.heading: `GET|POST /api/substances/products/`

sections.body: `GET` returns one product. `PATCH` changes `name`, `label_source` and `label_fetched_on`; a new `label_source` needs a new `label_fetched_on` in the same request (`400` otherwise). There is no delete route: protocol versions keep the product id.
sections.heading: `GET|PATCH /api/substances/products/<id>/`

sections.body: Adds one declared ingredient (`201`). The same substance twice on one product is `400`.
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/products/<id>/ingredients/`

sections.body: `PATCH` corrects `amount_per_unit`, `unit` and `label_source` (the substance cannot change; delete the row and add another); sending `amount_per_unit: null` and `unit: null` records that the label gives no amount. The result must still hold the rules above. `DELETE` removes the row (`204`).
sections.heading: `PATCH|DELETE /api/substances/products/<id>/ingredients/<ingredient_id>/`

sections.body: A synonym is `{id, substance, name, language, source, reviewer, reviewed_at}`. `language` is a BCP 47 tag kept as typed and `source` is required. Nothing is seeded and nothing is fetched from Wikidata or Evipedia (Q108). A name resolves only by exact match, after case-folding and whitespace collapsing, on a **reviewed** synonym of exactly one substance. Every other outcome is `ambiguous` and queued. Text fields refuse NUL characters and over-long values with `400`.
sections.heading: Synonyms and name resolution (TG-b)

sections.body: Staff only (`403` for others). `POST` takes `substance` (id), `name` (max 200), `language` (max 35) and `source` (max 300). `reviewer`, `reviewed_at` and `normalised_name` are set by the server: a request that sends one is `400`. The same name, language and substance twice is `400`. The new synonym is unreviewed.
sections.heading: `GET|POST /api/substances/synonyms/`

sections.body: Staff only. Sets `reviewer` to the requesting user and `reviewed_at` to now; a body is ignored. `400` if already reviewed.
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/synonyms/<id>/approve/`

sections.body: Staff only. Lists items with `status` `open` (default), `resolved` or `rejected` (`?status=`). An item has `submitted_name`, `language`, `reason` (`no_match`, `unreviewed_synonym`, `near_match`, `several_substances`, `no_code`: a reviewed synonym whose substance has no stored code), `candidate_substance_ids`, `status`, `resolved_by` and `resolved_substance`.
sections.heading: `GET /api/substances/review-queue/`

sections.body: Staff only. `resolve` takes `{substance: <id>}` and closes an open item with that substance, recording who did it; it does not create a synonym. `reject` closes it without one. A closed item gives `400`.
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/review-queue/<id>/resolve/` and `POST /api/substances/review-queue/<id>/reject/`

sections.body: Any signed-in user, throttled per user (scope `substance_resolve`, default 60/min, `SUBSTANCE_RESOLVE_THROTTLE_RATE`; `429` beyond it; Q125). A synonym counts as reviewed only while its reviewer account still exists (Q123). Body `{name, language?}`. Returns `{status, reason, substance, codes, review_item_id, candidates}`. `status` is `resolved` (with `substance` and its stored `codes`) or `ambiguous` (`substance` is `null`, `codes` empty, and the open queue item id is returned). Repeating a request reuses the open item. Near-match candidates use stdlib `difflib` with cutoff 0.8 over reviewed names and are only listed, never attached (Q117). `candidates` is filled only for staff users; for everyone else it is `[]` and only `review_item_id` is returned, so an unreviewed link never reaches end users. `language` is stored on the queue item and does not filter the match (Q118).
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/resolve/`

sections.body: All four routes below belong to the signed-in owner of the extraction: another user gets `404`, an anonymous request `401`. Nothing is attached to a protocol or substance, and no LLM or network call is made. The names are resolved by the same resolver as `/resolve/`, so each unresolved name also lands in the review queue.
sections.heading: Batch resolve and staged commit (TG-c)

sections.body:
Throttled per user (scope `substance_extraction`, default 60 names/min, `SUBSTANCE_EXTRACTION_THROTTLE_RATE`; `429` beyond it). Body `{entries: [{name, language?, proposed?}]}` with 1 to 50 entries (Q121); each entry uses one slot of the rate, so a batch of N names costs N (Q125). Returns `201` with `{id, created_at, committed_at, submitted, recognised, not_understood, items}`; the counts are computed by code and `submitted = recognised + not_understood`. Each item has `{id, submitted_name, language, status, substance, review_item_id, candidates, decision, decided_substance, decided_at, accepted_fields, notes, ambiguous}`. `status` is `resolved` (with `substance`) or `not_understood`. `candidates` (difflib near-matches, never resolved) is filled for staff only. Duplicate names are each counted and share one decision (Q120). A non-text name, an empty or over-long name (over 200), a NUL character or more than 50 entries is `400` and nothing is stored.

`proposed` is an optional `{field: value}` map from an extractor, checked by the constrained-column validator against `system`, `code` and `source` of the substance code model. A value is written to `accepted_fields` only if it is an exact member of the `system` enum or fits the field's maximum length. `notes` (free text, any length) goes to the item's `notes`. Any other value, an unknown field or a non-text value is listed in `ambiguous` as `{field, value, reason}` (`not_in_enum`, `too_long`, `not_text`, `unknown_field`) with the full original value, never truncated; the other fields and entries are still stored.
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/extractions/`

sections.body: Returns the same object as the submit response, with the current decisions.
sections.heading: `GET /api/substances/extractions/<id>/`

sections.body: Body `{decision: "corrected", substance: <id>}` or `{decision: "left_out"}`; only for a `not_understood` item of an uncommitted extraction (`400` otherwise, including an unknown substance). A correction is recorded with actor and time and creates no synonym (Q122). Can be changed until commit. Returns the item.
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/extractions/<id>/items/<item_id>/decide/`

sections.body: `400` with a plain message while any not-understood item has no decision, or if already committed. Otherwise sets `committed_at` and returns the extraction (Q124).
sections.heading: `POST /api/substances/extractions/<id>/commit/`

sections.body:
Searches the imported LOINC terms by name words or by LOINC code. Throttled per scope `loinc_search` (default `60/min`, `LOINC_SEARCH_THROTTLE_RATE`); over the limit: `429`.

- `q` is required, at most 200 characters after trimming. A missing, empty or too long `q`: `400` with a message under `q`.
- Paginated: `page`, and `page_size` (default 20, at most 100).
- `200` lists terms, each with `loinc_num`, `long_common_name`, `short_name`, `component`, `system`, `property`, `scale_type`, `status` and `source` (`name`, `version`, `licence`, `url`, `retrieved_at`).
sections.heading: `GET /api/terminology/loinc/?q=<text>`

sections.body:
Returns the ranges of one analyte, kept as three separate keys, each with its source: `reference`, `optimal` and `safety`, plus `biomarker` (`loinc_code`, `name`, `unit` as a UCUM code) and `value`. `optimal` is `null` unless its provenance is complete. Only `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` are allowed.

- Optional `?value=<decimal>`: each range then carries a `status` computed in code. The value is taken to be in the analyte's unit; no unit conversion is done. A value that is not a finite decimal: `400` with a message under `value`.
- An unknown `loinc_code`: `404`.
sections.heading: `GET /api/terminology/biomarkers/<loinc_code>/ranges/`
